skills.name: An article on cash crops and community life

note.text: An article informs a particular audience. Give it a suitable title, an introduction and organised paragraphs. Explain how a cash crop can contribute to income, jobs or trade, while recognising production costs, price uncertainty and possible effects on land use. Do not claim that every farmer earns the same income or that a crop removes all economic problems. Use original examples and checked facts rather than copying a source or inventing statistics.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: An article informs a particular audience. Give it a suitable title, an introduction and organised paragraphs. Explain how a cash crop can contribute to income, jobs or trade, while recognising production costs, price uncertainty and possible effects on land use. Do not claim that every farmer earns the same income or that a crop removes all economic problems. Use original examples and checked facts rather than copying a source or inventing statistics.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original model: Cash Crops and Our Community. An imaginary cocoa-growing community earns income when produce is sold. Transport and trading also create work. However, costs and changing prices affect what households retain. Food production and careful land use remain important. The community benefits most when people consider both opportunities and difficulties rather than assuming that every sale is pure profit.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: State the audience and main idea. Group related benefits and limitations in separate paragraphs and link them with clear connectives. Label invented examples as examples. Avoid turning an English article into unverified advice about crop treatment or investment.

model: Cash Crops and Our Community. An imaginary cocoa-growing community earns income when produce is sold. Transport and trading also create work. However, costs and changing prices affect what households retain. Food production and careful land use remain important. The community benefits most when people consider both opportunities and difficulties rather than assuming that every sale is pure profit.

I recognise costs or uncertainty and avoid unsupported statistics.
